ytShorts.label: SHORTS PIPELINE
ytShorts.title: Automatic daily Shorts production

steps.title: Topic pick
steps.desc: Picks a script that fits the day’s topic from a prepared set; never reuses the same content.

steps.title: Voice-over
steps.desc: Has an AI voice read the script and builds captions synced to the speech.

steps.title: Footage
steps.desc: Finds matching vertical footage on free stock sites; skips clips used recently.

steps.title: Editing
steps.desc: Combines footage, voice, music and captions into one vertical video.

steps.title: Thumbnail
steps.desc: Creates a thumbnail image from the video title.

steps.title: Upload
steps.desc: Uploads to YouTube, sets the publish time and sends a phone notification.

ytShorts.loop: Adjusts the publishing plan based on which times and topics get more views.
ytShorts.note: If a step fails, the job resumes where it stopped instead of starting over.
ytShorts.start: Starts on its own at a set time every day.
ytShorts.end: A Shorts video on YouTube with its publish time set.

ytLong.label: LONG VIDEO PIPELINE
ytLong.title: From one recording to a multilingual long video with chapters

steps.title: Recording
steps.desc: Speech and translation audio come from a licensed source.

steps.title: Speaker split
steps.desc: Splits the recording by speaker using pauses and voice tone.

steps.title: Timing
steps.desc: Transcribes the speech and finds when each word is spoken.

steps.title: Text matching
steps.desc: Matches the spoken part to the source text and its translation, fixing errors.

steps.title: Page design
steps.desc: Lays out the text and translation as readable pages; right-to-left scripts display correctly.

steps.title: Assembly
steps.desc: Joins intro, chapters, transitions and outro into one video, adding chapter markers and a thumbnail.

ytLong.note: Intro, transition and outro announcements are read by an AI voice.
ytLong.end: A multilingual long video with chapters and a thumbnail.

shoai.label: VIDEO SCRIPT GENERATOR
shoai.title: From a topic to a voiced video script
shoai.start: The user starts a new video from the dashboard.
shoai.end: A scene-by-scene video script with voice-over.

steps.title: Topic
steps.desc: Picks one of the ready-made topics or writes a custom one.

steps.title: Style and length
steps.desc: Sets the visual style (realistic, cartoon, anime…) and the video length (15 s – 1 min).

steps.title: Script
steps.desc: AI splits the video into scenes based on the choices and writes the narration for each.

steps.title: Visual brief
steps.desc: Writes a detailed visual brief for each scene: background, colors and camera angle.

steps.title: Voice-over
steps.desc: Each scene’s text is read by the chosen AI voice; voice settings are adjustable.

steps.title: Preview
steps.desc: Scenes are listed with their visual briefs and audio; each clip can be played on its own.

shoai.note: Choices are kept in the browser, so the form survives a page refresh.

zestify.label: RECIPE EXTRACTOR
zestify.title: From a cooking video to a saved recipe
zestify.start: The user pastes an Instagram Reels link into the app.
zestify.end: A recipe with ingredients and steps, saved to a personal collection.

steps.title: Link
steps.desc: The app checks the link and sends it to the server.

steps.title: Download
steps.desc: The server downloads the post’s video temporarily.

steps.title: Transcription
steps.desc: The audio is extracted and the speech is transcribed.

steps.title: Recipe extraction
steps.desc: AI filters out the chatter and pulls out the dish name, ingredients and steps. If the video has no recipe, it reads the post caption instead.

steps.title: Translation
steps.desc: The recipe is translated into the app’s language; frequent texts come from a cache.

steps.title: Saving
steps.desc: The recipe is saved to the account and the device; the same recipe is never added twice.

zestify.note: Video processing runs on the server; the phone only sends the link and shows the result.

aiclipper.label: CLIP EXTRACTOR
aiclipper.title: From a long stream to clips of its best moments
aiclipper.start: A long game stream or educational video is uploaded; content type and language are chosen.
aiclipper.end: Separate clip files, each named with its tag and score.

steps.title: Video and options
steps.desc: The video comes in from the command line or the API. Game stream, Rust stream or educational content is chosen.

steps.title: Transcription
steps.desc: Speech is transcribed with timestamps, using the graphics card when available.

steps.title: Chunking
steps.desc: The text is split into 30-second chunks that slightly overlap, so moments on a boundary aren't lost.

steps.title: Scoring moments
steps.desc: AI gives each moment a title, a tag and an importance score from 0 to 100. Chunks are processed in parallel.

steps.title: Merge and filter
steps.desc: Overlapping or similar moments are merged; those scoring below the threshold are dropped.

steps.title: Cutting clips
steps.desc: The user picks the moments they want; clips are cut quickly without re-encoding.

aiclipper.note: If the same video is processed again, analysis results come from the cache instead of asking the AI twice.

feedtune.label: FEED READER
feedtune.title: Websites and YouTube channels in a single feed
feedtune.start: The user pastes a website link or searches for a YouTube channel by name.
feedtune.end: New content from every source, in one feed you can save and filter.

steps.title: Site or channel
steps.desc: The link is checked; YouTube channels can be found by searching their name.

steps.title: Recognizing the source
steps.desc: The site's RSS feed is read for its name and category; a YouTube link is resolved to a channel ID.

steps.title: Fetching content
steps.desc: New posts and videos are fetched; YouTube Shorts are flagged separately.

steps.title: Finding images
steps.desc: The cover image comes from the feed; if missing, the article page's share image is used.

steps.title: Saving
steps.desc: Only new items are added and nothing is saved twice. Each user sees only their own data.

steps.title: One feed
steps.desc: Posts and videos share one feed; items can be favorited or saved for later, and navigated with keyboard shortcuts.

feedtune.loop: When the app opens, sources older than 30 minutes are refreshed. A weekly job also removes content older than 30 days, keeping favorites and saved items.

portfolioOs.label: PORTFOLIO SITE
portfolioOs.title: A portfolio that works like an operating system desktop
portfolioOs.end: A desktop with draggable windows, its content updated from an admin panel.

steps.title: Page
steps.desc: The page is rendered on the server, so it opens fast and search engines can read the content.

steps.title: Content
steps.desc: Profile, projects, experience and blog posts are read from the database in parallel and kept in memory for a few minutes.

steps.title: Windows
steps.desc: Each section is a window that can be dragged, resized and minimized, with a dock at the bottom.

steps.title: Personalization
steps.desc: Wallpaper and language can be changed; sleep mode opens a 3D screensaver.

steps.title: Contact
steps.desc: The contact form sends the email directly; repeated sends are rate limited.

steps.title: Admin panel
steps.desc: Content is added and edited from a password-protected panel; changes show up on the site right away.

portfolioOs.note: On small screens a simple tabbed view opens instead of the desktop. Five wrong passwords lock the panel for 15 minutes.

gabiflow.label: FORMS & WORKFLOW
gabiflow.title: Building forms and approval flows without code
gabiflow.start: A user opens a blank form and drags components into place.
gabiflow.end: The submitted form is written to the database by its events and reaches the next person.

steps.title: Drag-and-drop editor
steps.desc: Components are dragged from the toolbox onto a grid; rows and columns can be resized.

steps.title: Form components
steps.desc: Text box, dropdown, date, checkboxes, table and buttons, each configured from its own panel.

steps.title: Button events
steps.desc: Each button runs a sequence of events: an SQL query, a message to the user, a redirect, or sending the form to someone else.

steps.title: SQL and variables
steps.desc: Queries use @variables for form fields and the signed-in user; a query result can feed later events.

steps.title: Sending the form
steps.desc: The form is passed on with its values to another user, who opens it and completes their step. This builds an approval chain.

steps.title: Groups and sessions
steps.desc: Users are organized into groups. Sessions use JWT and passwords are stored with bcrypt.

gabiflow.note: Team project. Built for paperless processes; forms and events are stored in the database as JSON.
